title: PYTHON BASICS
tagline: Begin your coding quest and master the core foundations
description: Welcome to the enchanted kingdom of PyQuest! Awaken your magical coding potential as you learn Python syntax, manipulate elemental variables, and conjure interactive spells.

levels.title: Your First Python Program
levels.description: Master statement syntax, learn what Python is, and cast your very first print() invocation.

lessons.title: Your First Python Program
lessons.content:
Python is a programming language used to build applications, automate tasks, analyze data, and much more.

Python code is clean, readable, and written in plain English-like statements. In PyQuest, your Python code directly commands the computer to perform actions and solve challenges!
lessons.codeExample:
# Your first Python statement
print("Hello, Python!")
lessons.tip: Python code executes line by line from top to bottom.

lessons.title: The print() Function
lessons.content:
The `print()` function is the primary tool to output information to the console screen.

Whatever text you place inside `print(...)` surrounded by quotation marks will be displayed as output without the quotes!
lessons.codeExample:
print("Hello, Python!")
# Output displayed:
# Hello, Python!
lessons.tip: Always wrap your words in double quotes ("...") or single quotes ('...').

challenges.title: Output Prediction Trial
challenges.instructions: Inspect the Python code snippet below. What will be displayed on the console screen?
challenges.question: print("Hello Python")
hints: Remember that print() outputs the text inside the quotes, but does not print the quotation marks themselves.
challenges.explanation: Correct! The print() function displays the text content inside quotes. The quotation marks tell Python it is text, but are not printed.

challenges.title: Cast the print() Spell
challenges.instructions: Write a Python statement that prints the exact message 'Hello Python' to the console output.
challenges.starterCode: # Write your code below to print Hello Python
hints: Use the print() function: print("Hello Python")
challenges.explanation: Brilliant! You wrote and executed your very first Python program in the browser sandbox!

levels.title: Variables & Data
levels.description: Harness data containers: craft strings, store integers, measure floats, and balance booleans.

lessons.title: Variables: The Magic Jars
lessons.content: A variable is like a labeled container that stores data for later use. In Python, you create a variable by naming it and using the `=` assignment operator.
lessons.tip: Variable names in Python should use lowercase letters and underscores (snake_case).

challenges.title: Store Mana Power
challenges.instructions: Create a variable named `mana` and set it to `100`. Then print the value of `mana`.
challenges.starterCode: # Create mana variable and print it
challenges.explanation: Great job! Printing a variable without quotes displays the value held inside.

levels.title: User Input
levels.description: Communicate with users using input(), perform type conversions, and evaluate arithmetic expressions.

lessons.title: Gathering User Input
lessons.content: The `input()` function pauses execution and waits for the user to type something into the console. The user's input is returned as a text string.
lessons.tip: Remember that input() always returns text, so convert with int() if you need a number.

challenges.title: The Power Calculation
challenges.instructions: Read an integer number using `input()`, calculate its square, and print the result.
challenges.starterCode: # Read integer and print its square
challenges.explanation: Awesome! You handled dynamic standard input and computed numerical results!
